description: The Evaluation Dashboard provides dataset management, experiment tracking, and live LLM-as-judge evaluation. Two-panel layout: datasets/detail on the left, experiments/results on the right, with a lazy-loaded live evaluation tab.

groups.name: Dataset Management
groups.description: Users need to create, browse, select, and delete evaluation datasets. The dataset list is the entry point for all evaluation workflows â€” selecting a dataset populates the detail panel and scopes the experiment list. Datasets show name, version badge, item count, and last-updated date. Deletion requires a two-step confirmation (trash icon then Confirm/Cancel) to prevent accidental data loss.

assertions.description: The user sees the page heading 'Evaluation Dashboard' with the subtitle 'Manage datasets, run experiments, and review results' confirming they are on the correct page
The user sees a 'Datasets' section header in the left panel, establishing the dataset list area

The user can click the 'New Dataset' button to open an inline creation form with fields for 'Dataset Name' (placeholder 'e.g. Customer Support QA') and 'Description (optional)' (placeholder 'Brief description...')
When the create dataset form is open, the user sees 'Dataset Name' and 'Description (optional)' labels with 'Create' and 'Cancel' buttons, and the Create button is disabled until a name is entered
Each dataset row displays the dataset name, a version badge (e.g. 'v1'), item count (e.g. '42 items'), and formatted last-updated date, allowing the user to identify and compare datasets at a glance

Dataset deletion uses a two-step confirmation pattern: a trash icon reveals 'Confirm' and 'Cancel' buttons instead of immediately deleting, preventing accidental deletion of datasets and their associated experiments
assertions.precondition: At least one dataset exists in the list

assertions.description: When no datasets exist, the user sees a 'No datasets yet' message with a database icon, guiding them to create their first dataset
The user can click the 'Refresh' button in the top bar to reload all evaluation data
When dataset loading fails, the user sees 'Failed to load evaluation data' with the error message and a 'Retry' button to attempt recovery

groups.name: Dataset Items
groups.description: Once a dataset is selected, users need to view, add, import, export, and delete individual items. Items are displayed in a two-column table (Input / Expected Output). Users can add items by pasting a JSON array, importing a JSON or CSV file, or export existing items as JSON or CSV. Individual items can be deleted with a browser confirmation dialog.

assertions.description: The items table displays 'Input' and 'Expected Output' column headers, allowing the user to understand the structure of evaluation data
assertions.precondition: A dataset is selected and has at least one item

assertions.description: The items table shows an 'Expected Output' column so users can see the ground truth for each evaluation item
assertions.precondition: A dataset is selected and has at least one item

assertions.description: The user can click the 'Add Items' button to open a form for bulk-adding items to the dataset
assertions.precondition: A dataset is selected and has at least one item

assertions.description: The add items form contains a textarea labeled 'Paste JSON array of items' with a placeholder showing the expected format: objects with 'input' and 'expected_output' fields
assertions.precondition: A dataset is selected and has at least one item

assertions.description: The user can click 'Import File' to upload a .json or .csv file containing evaluation items, with CSV files expected to have 'input' and 'expected_output' header columns
assertions.precondition: A dataset is selected and has at least one item

assertions.description: When items exist in the dataset, the user can click the 'JSON' export button to download items as a formatted JSON file named after the dataset
assertions.precondition: A dataset is selected and has at least one item

assertions.description: When items exist in the dataset, the user can click the 'CSV' export button to download items as a CSV file with input and expected_output columns
assertions.precondition: A dataset is selected and has at least one item

assertions.description: Each item row has a trash icon button titled 'Delete item' that triggers a browser confirm dialog before removing the item from the dataset
assertions.precondition: A dataset is selected and has at least one item

assertions.description: When a dataset has no items, the user sees 'No items in this dataset' with guidance text 'Click "Add Items" to get started'
When no dataset is selected, the detail panel displays 'Select a dataset to view its items' guiding the user to pick a dataset first

criteria.textContent: Select a dataset to view its items

groups.name: Experiment Management
groups.description: Users create and browse experiments scoped to the selected dataset. Each experiment has a name, optional description, optional prompt variant ID, and a status badge (pending/running/completed/failed) with color coding. The experiment creation form appears inline with fields for name, description, and prompt variant ID. The experiment list shows completion progress (e.g. '3/10 completed') and creation date.

assertions.description: The right panel shows an 'Experiments' section header when the experiments tab is active

The user can click the 'New Experiment' button to open an inline creation form with fields for experiment name (placeholder 'Experiment name'), description (placeholder 'Description (optional)'), and prompt variant (placeholder 'Prompt Variant ID (optional)')
assertions.precondition: A dataset is selected

assertions.description: Each experiment displays a color-coded status badge â€” muted for 'pending', info/blue for 'running', green for 'completed', red for 'failed' â€” so users can immediately identify experiment progress
Each experiment row shows a completion fraction (e.g. '3/10 completed') indicating how many items have been evaluated out of the total, along with the creation date
When no dataset is selected, the experiment panel shows 'Select a dataset to view experiments' guiding the user to pick a dataset first

criteria.textContent: Select a dataset to view experiments

assertions.description: When a dataset has no experiments, the user sees 'No experiments yet' prompting them to create one

The experiment creation form has three input fields with placeholders 'Experiment name', 'Description (optional)', and 'Prompt Variant ID (optional)', plus a 'Create' button that is disabled until a name is entered
assertions.precondition: A dataset is selected

groups.name: Experiment Results
groups.description: When an experiment is selected, users see a detailed results view with summary cards at the top (average scores, total cost, total tokens, results count) and a paginated table below. The table shows Input, Output, Scores (as colored percentage badges), Duration, Cost, and Tokens columns. All numeric columns and individual score names are sortable. Pagination displays 20 results per page with Previous/Next buttons and a 'Showing X-Y of Z results' indicator.

assertions.description: The results view shows summary cards at the top with average score percentages for each metric, allowing users to quickly assess overall experiment quality
assertions.precondition: An experiment is selected and has at least one result

assertions.description: The summary section shows a 'Total Cost' card displaying the aggregate cost of running the experiment
assertions.precondition: An experiment is selected and has at least one result

assertions.description: The summary section shows a 'Total Tokens' card displaying the aggregate token usage for the experiment
assertions.precondition: An experiment is selected and has at least one result

assertions.description: The summary section shows a 'Results' card displaying the total number of evaluated items in the experiment
assertions.precondition: An experiment is selected and has at least one result

assertions.description: The results table has columns for Input, Output, Scores, Duration, Cost, and Tokens, with sortable headers for Duration, Cost, Tokens, and individual score names
assertions.precondition: An experiment is selected and has at least one result

assertions.description: The user can click the 'Duration' column header to sort results by execution time in ascending or descending order
assertions.precondition: An experiment is selected and has at least one result

assertions.description: The user can click the 'Cost' column header to sort results by cost in ascending or descending order
assertions.precondition: An experiment is selected and has at least one result

assertions.description: The user can click the 'Tokens' column header to sort results by token usage in ascending or descending order
assertions.precondition: An experiment is selected and has at least one result

assertions.description: Individual result scores are displayed as colored percentage badges â€” green for scores >= 80%, yellow/warning for >= 50%, red/danger for < 50% â€” allowing quick visual assessment of quality
assertions.precondition: An experiment is selected and has at least one result

assertions.description: When more than 20 results exist, the user sees pagination controls with 'Previous' and 'Next' buttons, a page indicator ('Page X of Y'), and a results range indicator ('Showing X-Y of Z results')
assertions.precondition: An experiment has more than 20 results

assertions.description: The pagination bar includes a 'Next' button to navigate forward through result pages
assertions.precondition: An experiment has more than 20 results

assertions.description: Each result row has an 'Evaluate' button that pre-fills the live evaluation panel with that row's input and output, switching to the Run Evaluation tab
assertions.precondition: An experiment is selected and has at least one result

assertions.description: When an experiment has no results, the user sees 'No results yet' with the guidance 'Results will appear as the experiment runs'
When no experiment is selected but a dataset is, the user sees 'Select an experiment to view results' guiding them to pick an experiment

criteria.textContent: Select an experiment to view results

assertions.description: When no dataset is selected, the results area shows 'Select a dataset first' indicating the user needs to start by choosing a dataset

groups.name: Live Evaluation
groups.description: The live evaluation panel (lazy-loaded under the 'Run Evaluation' tab) lets users run on-demand LLM-as-judge evaluations. Users provide an input (prompt/question), output (LLM response), and optional context (for RAG), select an eval spec (saved or inline JSON), and click Evaluate. Results show pass/fail badges per assertion with actual vs threshold percentages and explanatory messages. A Reset button clears the form and results.

assertions.description: The user can switch to the 'Run Evaluation' tab in the right panel to access the live evaluation form
assertions.precondition: At least one eval spec exists in the system

assertions.description: The live evaluation panel header shows the description 'Evaluate an input/output pair using LLM-as-judge assertions' explaining the panel's purpose

criteria.textContent: Evaluate an input/output pair using LLM-as-judge assertions

assertions.precondition: At least one eval spec exists in the system

assertions.description: The user can choose between 'Saved' and 'Inline JSON' eval spec modes â€” Saved shows a dropdown with 'Select an eval spec...' placeholder, Inline JSON shows a textarea for custom spec JSON
assertions.precondition: At least one eval spec exists in the system

assertions.description: The user can click the 'Saved' toggle button to switch to the saved eval spec selection mode with a dropdown
assertions.precondition: At least one eval spec exists in the system

assertions.description: The user can click the 'Inline JSON' toggle button to switch to the inline JSON spec entry mode
assertions.precondition: At least one eval spec exists in the system

assertions.description: The user sees an 'Input (prompt / question)' labeled textarea with placeholder 'Enter the prompt or question that was sent to the LLM...' for entering the evaluation input
assertions.precondition: At least one eval spec exists in the system

assertions.description: The user sees an 'Output (LLM response)' labeled textarea with placeholder 'Enter the LLM response to evaluate...' for entering the response to judge
assertions.precondition: At least one eval spec exists in the system

assertions.description: The user sees an optional 'Context' labeled textarea with '(optional, for RAG)' annotation and placeholder 'Provide grounding context if evaluating RAG responses...' for RAG evaluation scenarios
assertions.precondition: At least one eval spec exists in the system

assertions.description: The user can click the 'Evaluate' button to run the evaluation, which is disabled until both input and output are provided and an eval spec is selected. While running, it shows 'Evaluating...' with a spinner
assertions.precondition: At least one eval spec exists in the system

assertions.description: After results are displayed, the user can click 'Reset' to clear all form fields, results, and start a fresh evaluation
assertions.precondition: At least one eval spec exists in the system

assertions.description: Each assertion result shows a 'Pass' or 'Fail' badge with green check or red X icon, the assertion type name, actual vs threshold percentage (e.g. '85% / 70%'), and an explanatory message
assertions.precondition: At least one eval spec exists in the system

assertions.description: The results section shows a summary badge indicating how many assertions passed out of the total (e.g. '3/5 passed') with color coding â€” green when all pass, red when none pass, yellow for partial
assertions.precondition: At least one eval spec exists in the system

assertions.description: When evaluation fails, the user sees an 'Evaluation failed' error message with details about what went wrong
assertions.precondition: At least one eval spec exists in the system

assertions.description: When evaluation returns zero assertions, the user sees 'No assertions were evaluated. Check your eval spec configuration.' indicating a spec configuration issue
assertions.precondition: At least one eval spec exists in the system

groups.name: Cross-Panel Navigation
groups.description: The Evaluation Dashboard uses a two-panel layout where selecting items in one panel drives content in others. Selecting a dataset populates the detail panel with items and scopes the experiment list. Selecting an experiment populates the results panel. Clicking 'Evaluate' on a result row switches to the Run Evaluation tab and pre-fills the input/output fields. Tab switching between 'Experiments' and 'Run Evaluation' controls what the right panel displays.

assertions.description: Selecting a dataset highlights it with a primary-colored border and populates the detail panel below with that dataset's items, replacing the 'Select a dataset to view its items' placeholder

criteria.textContent: Select a dataset to view its items

assertions.description: Selecting a dataset scopes the experiment list to show only experiments for that dataset, and clears any previously selected experiment

criteria.textContent: Select a dataset to view experiments

assertions.description: Selecting an experiment highlights it and populates the results panel below with that experiment's results, summary cards, and pagination

criteria.textContent: Select an experiment to view results

assertions.description: The 'Evaluate' button on a result row switches the right panel from the Experiments tab to the Run Evaluation tab and pre-fills the input and output fields with that row's data
The user can click the 'Experiments' tab to switch the right panel back to the experiments list and results view

groups.name: Behavior â€” Multi-Step Workflows
groups.description: End-to-end behavioral assertions verifying that multi-step user workflows complete correctly: creating a dataset then adding items, running a live evaluation through the full form flow, exporting and importing data files, and deleting datasets with confirmation.

assertions.description: Creating a dataset and then adding items is a two-step workflow: a new dataset must be created first, after which items can be added to it via the JSON paste form

target.label: Two-step dataset creation then add items

assertions.description: A live evaluation requires an input, output, and eval spec selection before evaluation can run. Results display as assertion Pass/Fail badges in the results section
JSON export produces a downloadable file named after the dataset containing a valid JSON array of items with 'input' and 'expected_output' fields
Importing a .json or .csv file parses the file contents and adds the items to the dataset, which appear in the items table without requiring a page refresh
Dataset deletion uses a two-step confirmation flow. After confirmation, the dataset is removed from the list and the detail panel resets to the 'Select a dataset' placeholder

groups.name: State Consistency â€” Data Correctness
groups.description: Assertions verifying that displayed data is consistent across panels, matches backend state, and updates reactively after mutations. Covers item counts, experiment status badges, optimistic table updates after add/delete, pagination math, and score value accuracy.

assertions.description: The dataset item count displayed in the dataset list (e.g. '42 items') matches the actual number of rows rendered in the items table in the detail view

target.label: Dataset list item count vs detail table row count

assertions.description: The experiment status badge color and text (pending/running/completed/failed) matches the backend state â€” muted for 'pending', info for 'running', green for 'completed', red for 'failed'

target.label: Experiment status badge matches backend state

assertions.description: After adding items via JSON paste or file import, the items table updates immediately to show the new items without requiring a manual page refresh

target.label: Items table updates after add without refresh

assertions.description: After confirming deletion of a dataset item, the item row is removed from the items table immediately without requiring a page refresh

target.label: Deleted item removed from table immediately

assertions.description: The pagination controls show 'Page X of Y' where Y equals Math.ceil(totalResults / 20), and the 'Showing A-B of C results' range is consistent with the total result count and current page

target.label: Pagination page numbers consistent with total results

assertions.description: Score percentage values displayed in the results table badges (e.g. 'accuracy: 85%') match the actual numeric values returned by the evaluation backend

target.label: Score badge values match evaluation output

groups.name: Element Presence â€” Critical UI Elements
groups.description: Assertions verifying that critical UI elements are present and correctly structured in the rendered DOM. Covers dataset row composition, experiment row badges, results table column headers, live evaluation input areas, and pagination indicators.

assertions.description: Each dataset row in the list contains both the dataset name as a text label and an item count indicator (e.g. '42 items'), ensuring users can identify and compare datasets

target.label: Dataset row has name and item count

assertions.description: Each experiment row in the list contains a status badge element displaying one of the status values: pending, running, completed, or failed
The experiment results table contains column headers for Input, Output, Scores, Duration, Cost, and Tokens, providing the complete set of evaluation data dimensions

target.label: Results table has all required column headers

assertions.description: The live evaluation panel contains all three input textareas: 'Input (prompt / question)' for the prompt, 'Output (LLM response)' for the response, and 'Context' with '(optional, for RAG)' annotation for grounding context

target.label: Live eval has Input, Output, and Context areas

assertions.description: The pagination bar displays a 'Page X of Y' text indicator showing the current page number and total page count, positioned between the Previous and Next buttons

target.label: Pagination shows Page X of Y indicator
